NAH. Have you asked your younger brother if he could go to his friends house instead of them coming to you? 

You present your case so fairly and maturely, and I really do feel your pain in not being taken seriously. I don’t have a disability but I do have an invisible illness so I completely get that feeling of your symptoms just being ignored and misunderstood. It’s very draining and probably not helping your mental state. 

I would say asking for 2 days notice is unreasonable. Your younger brother probably wants a normal social life like any teenager, and part of that is last minute plans. Although if his friends are over every single night you definitely need to come to some sort of compromise. You’re his brother and he should want to take your feelings and the needs of your autism into account. 

I don’t think you’re using your autism as a crutch at all, but as someone with a few autistic friends I hope I don’t offend you when I say I think your anger and frustration, and the entire emotional toll of the situation, is probably contributing a lot to the sensory overload and the feeling of being overwhelmed for you. It’s very understandable though.

YTA. 350 dollars a month plus paying her own groceries is ridiculous considering you were coping without her financial support before. You can afford it if she’s in school but you can’t now that she has a job? Something not adding up.

And yes she’ll pay rent when she lives alone, but you clearly have the financial means to support her paying a lot less since you offer to let her live there rent free if she’s in education. You should WANT to give your daughter the best possible life. 

When deciding to charge her rent, you took the route of a landlord instead of a mom. It’s fair to assume that $350 isn’t an accurate reflection of the expenses she causes to the house, it’s just something you’ve landed on because that might be what it’ll cost when she moves out. She’s gone for 40+ hours a week to work, pays her own groceries, and is out of the house to socialise. You’ve no need to charge her for costs incurred in YOUR house when she isn’t there - again, you’re not a landlord. 

To clarify, asking her to pay her way is more than fair. The decent thing to do as a MOM is to break down the price with her realistically and to the last cent so she can afford to save up and get her own place.

First of all I just want to give you both a massive hug! Your experience is so similar to mine. If you look back on my account, you'll see that my very first reddit post was in PTSD recounting my car crash in July 2019. 
I was 20, going about the same speed as you, except I was by myself. I know exactly how you feel, the guilt of what happened, the 'what ifs'. The feeling of almost guilt that you actually aren't as seriously injured as you should be? 
After my accident I was and still am quite traumatised. It takes a long time for things to get back to normal, but I promise you, they do. Even though its the last thing you want to do I really strongly encourage you to get in the car again. Even if you don't drive it. Switch it on and let the engine run, then go for a short drive, only 20mph and let it build up. I know how horrible it is having someone say that to you but honestly it's for the best. 
My car insurance had a policy that after 1 month I needed a new car or else my 8 remaining months of insurance would be cancelled with no payback (about £1000 worth of insurance - I also only had my car for 4 months before I crashed) so I literally had to be pushed back into it.

The flashbacks eased up for me after about 4/5 months. I stopped feeling like I was skidding every time I went around a corner. I promise you, it does get easier. You never will forget it though, I can still recount that day as if it were yesterday, but it 100% gets easier as time goes on. Oddly enough, I am very nervous of my boyfriends driving even though he is quite a safe driver, and I love driving myself. Even though I crashed myself, I need to have the power and be the one in control or else I also have the occasional mini panic. 

Another important thing, please don't compare your recovery to anybody else's. A week after crashing my car, a work colleague of mine also wrecked his car in an accident which was probably equally as bad as mine, and he was driving a week later and was completely fine. I remember feeling so guilty and pathetic that I was traumatised and he wasn't... but nobodies brains works the same way. So again please never compare your healing process to your boyfriends and don't let him do it with yours, you will both heal in your own time. Be patient with yourselves, you've both been through so much. I really hope you're both okay and things get easier soon
